public_rationale: The gist holds. Before the post, Core Scientific reported $24.4 million of 2024 HPC hosting revenue out of $510.7 million, under 5%. It ended 2024 with 16.5 MW of HPC critical IT load, about 3% of the 500+ MW tied to CoreWeave. Most of that capacity was still to be built, with 250 MW targeted for end-2025. So the operating AI capacity was small next to the headline deal. But the strongest wording, 'little proof' of 'any meaningful compute capacity at all', overstates the record. The company had publicly documented a specific operating 16.5 MW HPC site in Austin, earning revenue from CoreWeave. That is clear proof of real capacity, even if small. The result turns on what counts as 'meaningful', which he did not define.
limitations: Megawatt figures come from a third-party transcript of the earnings call, not the 10-K itself.
Whether 16.5 MW is 'meaningful' is a judgment; an informed reader could rate it either way.
Core Scientific hosts CoreWeave's GPUs rather than owning compute, which makes 'compute capacity' loose.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The author can find little proof that Core Scientific has any meaningful compute capacity at all.
conditions: based on the author's own search

statement.excerpt: In fact, I can find little proof that Core Scientific has any meaningful compute capacity at all.

from_speaker: context: CoreWeave's S-1 cites a deal for "more than 500 MW of capacity"
context: he cites $24.3 million of 2024 HPC hosting revenue from the 10-K
our_interpretation: The claim is about what the public record showed when he wrote, not about his private search. Plain reading: as of mid-March 2025, public evidence showed little or no meaningful operating AI or HPC capacity at Core Scientific, compared with the 500+ MW it was said to offer CoreWeave.

'Meaningful' is judged against the post's own framing, the 500+ MW contract. It is not judged by whether any capacity existed. The words 'at all' still mean that clear proof of a real, operating HPC site cuts against the strongest part of the sentence.
Core Scientific hosts CoreWeave's GPUs in its data centers; it does not own the GPUs. 'Compute capacity' is read as operating HPC data-center capacity, the sense the post uses.
Target period: FY2024, the period covered by the 10-K he cites, through the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Disclosures available by 2025-03-17 show Core Scientific's operating HPC capacity was small next to the 500+ MW contract, with most capacity still to be built or converted.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Disclosures available by 2025-03-17 show substantial operating HPC capacity, such as a large share of the 500 MW already energized and billing, or a clear, documented operating HPC site that makes 'little proof... at all' untenable.

evidence.publisher: Core Scientific (via Business Wire, republished by Silicon UK)
evidence.explanation: HPC hosting was under 5% of 2024 revenue; bitcoin mining was the rest. This supports the gist that operating AI/HPC capacity was small relative to the headline deal.
